_comment: Warm-white LED: the lit, diffused face of an LED panel, strip or bulb at about 3000 K. Emissive: its defining observable is that it glows, warm. The matter under the glow is the milky polycarbonate diffuser (its colour and gloss show only where the glow is dimmed). Param-only. Carries every relevant wear layer at 0 (C1): scratches (overlay 1, damage), dust as a deposit (Phase10), fingerprints, gated by the Grime mask; the master's emission is a constant the layers do not reach, so wear shows only on the diffuser's reflection, not in the glow. Built by the Phase11 batch. Reevaluate (2026-10-05, Phase12 click 5, the lead's pass): COLOUR-ONLY. A light's colour is a Creator port now (emission_color), and LED_CoolWhite with that port set to this article's 1.0, 0.456, 0.147 renders the same picture as this article in USDLiveView's renderer, Blender and Unreal. Kept as authored; not retired, renamed or deleted.
name: LED_WarmWhite_Clean_Base_s01_v01

sources.note: Only specular_ior is taken, for the polycarbonate diffuser: the entry is the clear resin, not a milky diffuser.

sources.why: emission_color 1.0, 0.456, 0.147 is a 3000 K blackbody in linear sRGB (sRGB about 255, 180, 107), the common warm-white LED; emission_luminance 12 matches the library's other emitter (Neon_Signage) on the rig's relative scale, not measured nits. The diffuser under it is a milky polycarbonate (base 0.80, 0.80, 0.78, roughness 0.3). Physically Based's materials list has no LED or light entry.
